headline: 657 dead as measles outbreak hits Bangladesh
summary: The DGHS reports 10,523 confirmed cases and over 87,000 suspected cases, with Dhaka Division recording the highest number of deaths.
details: A child with measles symptoms died in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 657. According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 93 people have died of confirmed measles since March 15, while 564 have died with suspected symptoms.
In the last 24 hours alone, 136 new cases were detected and 1,006 people visited hospitals with symptoms, of which 938 were admitted.
The Dhaka Division has been the hardest hit, recording 239 deaths, followed by Rajshahi with 87 deaths.
Since the start of the outbreak, Bangladesh has recorded 10,523 confirmed cases of measles, though the suspected caseload is significantly higher at 87,929.
To combat the spread, the Holy Family Red Crescent has launched Bangladesh's first measles treatment guideline to improve clinical management of the disease.

headline: US Ambassador impressed by Rajshahi mangoes during market visit
summary: Ambassador Brent T. Christensen visited the Baneshwar mango market in Puthia, praising the fruit's quality and suggesting cold chain improvements for exports.
details: US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent T. Christensen visited the Baneshwar mango market in Puthia, Rajshahi, on Tuesday. He toured various stalls and warehouses, tasting fresh mangoes and learning about the different varieties available.

The Ambassador expressed his delight, noting that while he had visited Rajshahi in 2020, this was his first official visit as Ambassador. He mentioned coming from an agricultural state in the US and emphasized the value of experiencing products at their source.

Regarding export potential, Christensen stated that Americans love mangoes, but typically only have access to frozen ones used in shakes or food products. He noted that fresh Bangladeshi mangoes are not easily available in the US.

To increase exports, the Ambassador highlighted the need for improved cold chain and modern refrigeration systems. He stated that frozen mangoes are highly suitable for international markets and that infrastructure development is essential to ensure year-round availability.

Local traders at the market expressed pride in the Ambassador's visit, hoping that his interest would bring more international recognition and increase the demand for Rajshahi mangoes in foreign markets.
caption:
From the US to Rajshahi: The American Ambassador tastes fresh mangoes and calls for better cold chains to boost exports.

US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent T. Christensen visited the Baneshwar mango market in Puthia, Rajshahi, on Tuesday. He toured various stalls and warehouses, tasting fresh mangoes and learning about the different varieties available.

The Ambassador expressed his delight, noting that while he had visited Rajshahi in 2020, this was his first official visit as Ambassador. He mentioned coming from an agricultural state in the US and emphasized the value of experiencing products at their source.

Regarding export potential, Christensen stated that Americans love mangoes, but typically only have access to frozen ones used in shakes or food products. He noted that fresh Bangladeshi mangoes are not easily available in the US.

To increase exports, the Ambassador highlighted the need for improved cold chain and modern refrigeration systems. He stated that frozen mangoes are highly suitable for international markets and that infrastructure development is essential to ensure year-round availability.

Local traders at the market expressed pride in the Ambassador's visit, hoping that his interest would bring more international recognition and increase the demand for Rajshahi mangoes in foreign markets.

Source: Jamuna TV, Somoy News, Prothom Alo
